reader.requirement: At 1985 a level-88 condition-name entry has no true level: it neither subdivides, opens nor closes a group and occupies no storage, so it is associated with the entry it immediately follows (elementary, group or 77) wherever it is written, and the level hierarchy around it continues as if it were absent.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85 (refute-1985-c01/src). rlv1 (runs/rlv1-001): 88s on an OCCURS group and on its subordinate leave the table at LT=08 and each entry at LTE=02, subscripted condition-names test and SET per occurrence (O1=Y O2=N A3=Y, T2=131313FZ); an 88 on a FILLER tests its value (FF=Y); 88s on a REDEFINES group and its subordinate leave R1 at 3; a 66 RENAMES written after the record's last 88 spans R1A THRU R1C (LRN=03 RN=ABC); a sequential FD record with 88s at three depths is written by SET and read back at length 4 (FR=OKNO FOK=Y). rlvr1 versus rlvr1b: an 88 between 05 A and 03 B under G does not hide the unequal level-numbers, the same COBOL2771 citing §1985:IV.4.3.2.1 with and without it. rlvr2: an 88 after a 66 refused COBOL1976 (GR2 b). rlvr3: an 88 on a group holding a COMP item refused COBOL1976 citing the 1985-only exclusion GR2 c. rlvr4: an 88 on an index item refused; an 88 indented under another 88 is associated with the same conditional variable, as GR2 a requires. cite.py: OK §1985:IV.4.3.2.1 GR3; OK §1985:VI.5.3.4 GR2; OK §1985:IV.4.3.2.1 (p2, the identical-level rule).
